origins.section: 17.2 How the Processor Ends Decides Where the File Goes
17.4 A Stop or a Crash Leaves Files in `run/`, Some of Them Already Done
17.5 A Command Sees Only the JVM It Runs In
17.6 `drift` Shows a Pause Only When It Covers the Monitor's Wake-Up

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-retry-stalls-pool: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retry-stalls-pool: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-retry-stalls-pool: 17.2 says a retry makes the pool thread wait ten poll intervals (here 10 x 2000 ms = 20 s) and shows that with poolSize 1 a file stuck in retry adds up to that wait to every file behind it, so the reader reaches b.
recorded.prompt:q-sigterm-run-dir: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-sigterm-run-dir: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-sigterm-run-dir: 17.4 says the poller moves every file to run/ from its first listing, the SIGTERM shutdown 'doesn't wait for the pool', the pool goes on taking queued files until the JVM exits, and a longer grace period doesn't help, so the reader reaches c.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-second-jvm: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-second-jvm: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-probe-second-jvm: 17.5 shows that -c starts a second JVM with its own registry, deployed from deploy-cli/, and ops:muxstat through -c prints 'no MUX in this JVM' while a link is down, so the probe never sees DOWN, which gives d.
recorded.prompt:q-drift-misses-pause: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-drift-misses-pause: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-drift-misses-pause: 17.6 shows that drift measures only how late the monitor woke, that the part of a pause inside its sleep goes unmeasured, and that the next dump after a noon pause says 'drift : 0', so a 12:03 pause gives about 0 ms at 12:10, which is c.

recorded.prompt:q-retry-stalls-pool:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retry-stalls-pool:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-retry-stalls-pool:a: 17.2 says outright that the ten-interval wait 'also happens on a pool thread', not on the polling thread.
recorded.prompt:q-retry-stalls-pool:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retry-stalls-pool:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-retry-stalls-pool:c: 17.2 says 'DirPoll keeps no count of attempts' and the file goes round until a person moves it, so nothing moves it to bad/ after a third retry.
recorded.prompt:q-retry-stalls-pool:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-retry-stalls-pool:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-retry-stalls-pool:d: The 17.2 timeline shows c1-c3 processed between b2's retries, so they are delayed rather than held until the file is fixed; the 'name order' claim is never addressed, but the reader can reject the conclusion without it. This option is partly true, because the files are held, just not indefinitely.
recorded.prompt:q-sigterm-run-dir:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-sigterm-run-dir:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-sigterm-run-dir:a: 17.4 says the shutdown hook undeploys the adaptor, which stops the polling thread 'but doesn't wait for the pool', and run/ still holds three files after SIGTERM.
recorded.prompt:q-sigterm-run-dir:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-sigterm-run-dir:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-sigterm-run-dir:b: 17.4 shows run/ still holding b1, b2 and b4 after a SIGTERM exit and says nothing moves files back from run/, so the runbook has to do it.
recorded.prompt:q-sigterm-run-dir:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-sigterm-run-dir:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-sigterm-run-dir:d: 17.4 says the pool 'went on taking files from its queue while Q2 shut down' and b1 was posted yet left in run/, which refutes both the stop and the rollback. This option is partly true, because 'several files' is the right outcome; only the reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-second-jvm:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-second-jvm:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-probe-second-jvm:a: 17.5 says the command started a second JVM with its own registry, so its NameRegistrar does not hold the node's MUXes.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-second-jvm:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-second-jvm:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-probe-second-jvm:b: 17.5 says that with -c and no -d, Q2 deploys deploy-cli/ instead of deploy/, and that only the logger is deployed there.
recorded.prompt:q-probe-second-jvm:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-probe-second-jvm:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-probe-second-jvm:c: 17.5 shows an operator running -c in the node's directory while the node runs, and it executes (shownr, shutdown), so it is not refused. This option is partly true, because 'nothing wrong' is the right outcome; only the reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-drift-misses-pause:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-drift-misses-pause:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-drift-misses-pause:a: 17.6 defines drift as how late the monitor woke up, and the 3011 ms pause reported as 531 shows that it adds nothing up.
recorded.prompt:q-drift-misses-pause:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-drift-misses-pause:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-drift-misses-pause:b: 17.6's example shows that the 2.5 s of the pause that fell inside the sleep did not delay the wake-up ('nothing measures them'), so a pause that ends minutes before the wake-up adds nothing.
recorded.prompt:q-drift-misses-pause:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-drift-misses-pause:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-drift-misses-pause:d: 17.6 names 'a garbage collection pause, or a process starved of CPU' as causes of a late wake-up, so GC is not left out. This option is partly true, because 'about 0 ms' is the right number; only the reason is wrong.
